_about: PROTOTYPE (tools/): the claim-sheet date trial. Fabricated claim sheets whose dates are written the many ways people write them; candidate reading rules are scored on how many dates they read correctly, read WRONG (the worst outcome) or leave for the officer. Not used by the application.
_writer_styles: Share of sheets written in each style. mixed_words_and_numbers: one person, one order, some dates with month words and some without.
_order_swapper_share: Share of numeric sheets whose writer swaps day and month on some rows (inconsistent sheet).
_ocr_noise: Sheets read from a PDF picture get OCR-like confusions (O for 0, l for 1, S for 5, a stray space) on this share of their dates.
_receipts: For receipt evidence: a row's true date is on its receipt with this probability; the swapped reading coincidentally appears on a receipt with the same amount with the coincidence rate.
_max_claim_span_days: Chronology check: a reading that spreads the sheet's dates over more days than this is implausible for one claim.
_excel: excel_locale_swapped (added 2026-09-24 after a real workbook showed it): a writer typing into an Excel set to the other day/month order. excel_dotted_text_rate: share of cells in correct Excel sheets typed as dotted text dates, which Excel never converts.
_processing_delay_days: How long after the last receipt the officer checks the claim: [from, to, share]. Claims are monthly; the owner's own July receipts were checked in September, so late checks are included.
